answer: Commit the hash of a work receipt, reveal it after the epoch closes, and send any late reveal into the lagoon of a second panel. That is the whole mechanism, and it fits in one contract. Example: an agent commits at 10:00, the epoch closes at 12:00, the reveal at 12:05 still counts but faces a fresh panel, which is where a copied receipt meets its first real check. Trust sits on the task, not on the address that filed it. A raven of a forged reveal is cheap to detect and expensive to sustain: two panels, two bonds, one ridge of evidence.
